content: The diagnosis of Post-Bariatric Surgery Hypoglycemia (PBSH) requires a thorough evaluation of the patient’s medical history, dietary habits, and activity levels. It is also essential to rule out other potential causes of hypoglycemia, such as malnutrition, adverse effects of medications, dumping syndrome, or the presence of an insulinoma. The initial management of PBSH focuses on dietary modifications. Patients are advised to consume carbohydrates that are absorbed more slowly, along with adequate amounts of protein and healthy fats, to help stabilize blood glucose levels and prevent rapid drops in glucose. Nutritional therapy provided by dietitians who have expertise in managing PBSH is strongly recommended. Additionally, the use of real-time continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) devices can be particularly helpful, especially for patients who experience hypoglycemia unawareness. In cases where dietary adjustments alone are insufficient, pharmacological interventions may be considered. Medications such as acarbose can be used to slow the absorption of carbohydrates. Alternatively, diazoxide or octreotide may be prescribed to reduce the secretion of glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) and insulin, thereby mitigating hypoglycemic episodes.
